verdicts.title: The documented 'Unamplified BLT/BandMF' accounting recipe silently prices a 1-step single-participation mechanism (MfGaussian defaults n_steps=1) for runs the same page describes as 5000-10000 steps
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end. _mf_gaussian.py:52-64 declares n_steps=1, min_sep=1, max_participations=None, and _effective_max_participations falls back to n_steps, so a bare mf_gaussian(nm, strategy) prices a one-step, single-participation Gaussian. Measured exactly the reporter's numbers with 'uv run python': mf_gaussian(1.0, blt_strategy(max_buffers=10)) has n_steps=1/min_sep=1/max_participations=None and epsilon_at(1e-5)=4.37717809602987; the same strategy at the page's own multi-epoch noise context (n_steps=5000, min_sep=100, max_participations=5) gives 28.15909094329467 (6.4x higher), and at the page's other noise context (n_steps=10000, min_sep=1) sensitivity is 100.0 and epsilon is inf, with the optimizer printing 'BLT has near-zero output_scale parameters'. No warning is emitted on the bare call. The docs citations are accurate: blt.md:164-167 is the bare call under '# Unamplified BLT' with an assert that reads as validation, blt.md:177-180 falsely states mf_gaussian populates min_sep and max_participations 'from ... the participation pattern' (there is none to read), and the same bare pattern recurs at docs/reference/accounting.md:409 (band_mf section), :427-428, and docs/user-guide/accounting.md:291-292. Checked for mitigations and found none: there is no docs-snippet execution anywhere in .github/workflows (docs.yml only builds/deploys mkdocs), so nothing pins or exercises these examples; the other mf_gaussian(1.0, strategy) occurrences in those files are wrapped in amplifiers, which supply their own participation context and are correct. Direction is non-conservative (under-reported epsilon) on a copy-pasteable recipe repeated in three user-facing pages, so high stands. Not covered by any open tracked issue: #319 concerns code-side DP-FTRL invariants, #324/#416 (docs-example execution) are closed, #417 is about benchmark numbers.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user copies the 'Unamplified BLT' recipe (blt.md:164-167, repeated at reference/accounting.md:409 and :427-428 and user-guide/accounting.md:291-292) to price a real run. Because MfGaussian defaults n_steps=1/min_sep=1/max_participations=None, the call silently returns the PLD of a single-step, single-participation Gaussian: measured epsilon_at(1e-5)=4.3772, versus 28.1591 for the participation context the same page's noise example uses (n_steps=5000, min_sep=100, max_participations=5) -- a 6.4x under-report -- and versus inf for the page's n_steps=10000, min_sep=1 example. The adjacent note reinforces the error by claiming the structural fields including min_sep and max_participations are populated from the participation pattern, and the assert eps > 0 and eps < inf makes the wrong number look validated. Nothing executes these snippets in CI.

verdicts.title: Both accounting namespace tables and two reference sections document six opaque.dpftrl.accounting factories that do not exist
verdicts.reasoning: Verified directly. packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/dpftrl/accounting/__init__.py declares __all__ = ['b_min_sep', 'balls_in_bins', 'mf_gaussian', 'per_step', 'poisson'] and imports only b_min_sep, balls_in_bins, mf_gaussian, poisson from opaque.api.accounting.dpftrl. Measured: hasattr is False for every one of band_mf, blt, bisr, bsr, lambda_cgd, identity_mf, and True for mf_gaussian/poisson/b_min_sep/balls_in_bins. The doc citations check out: docs/user-guide/accounting.md:20 and docs/reference/accounting.md:38 both list the six phantom names in the opaque.dpftrl.accounting row, docs/reference/accounting.md:396 still carries '### band_mf(noise_multiplier, sensitivity, coefficients) -> DpProcess' with a full parameter list (its own code block ironically calls mf_gaussian), :413 carries '### blt(noise_multiplier, sensitivity, gram_matrix=()) -> DpProcess', and prose at reference/accounting.md:352 and docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/band-mf.md:156 still names dpftrl_acc.band_mf. Failure is loud (AttributeError), so no epsilon impact; the reporter's affects_epsilon=false is correct. Severity kept at medium rather than low because this is the canonical API reference and the drift spans four locations including two full stale signature sections, one of which advertises a hand-passed sensitivity argument that the current single-source-of-truth API deliberately removed. Not a duplicate of an open issue: the umbrella #324 and its 'execute documentation examples and validate public factory signatures' child #416 are both closed, so this is residual drift that survived that work.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A reader of docs/reference/accounting.md:396 or :413 writes dpftrl_acc.band_mf(nm, sensitivity, coefficients) or dpftrl_acc.blt(...) from the published signature and gets AttributeError, because the façade exports only b_min_sep, balls_in_bins, mf_gaussian, per_step, poisson. The same six phantom names (band_mf, blt, bisr, bsr, lambda_cgd, identity_mf) are advertised in the namespace tables at docs/user-guide/accounting.md:20 and docs/reference/accounting.md:38, and prose at reference/accounting.md:352 and band-mf.md:156 still refers to dpftrl_acc.band_mf. The stale signatures additionally teach a hand-passed sensitivity argument that the mf_gaussian(nm, strategy) API removed to keep noise and accounting on one source of truth. The error is loud, so no privacy number is affected.

verdicts.title: BLT min-sep sensitivity precondition is violated at the DEFAULT momentum=1.0 as soon as an lr_schedule is attached, which the trainer does automatically -- reported sensitivity 1.45-1.54x too small at min_sep=1
verdicts.reasoning: The numerical claim reproduces exactly. I re-derived the true sensitivity by exhaustive enumeration of every min-sep-respecting participation set against the lower-triangular Toeplitz C built from _blt_toeplitz_coefs, and got, at max_buffers=10 and momentum=1.0: n=20/min_sep=1 with no schedule 4.47214 vs 4.47214 (ratio 1.0000); with linear_schedule(1.0, 0.0, 20) coefficient min -0.160402, reported 1.86202 vs true 2.69864 (ratio 1.4493); with cosine_schedule coefficient min -0.183244, reported 1.75101 vs true 2.69688 (ratio 1.5402). At min_sep=2 the ratios collapse to 1.0001 and at min_sep=3 to 1.0000. So the theorem precondition (non-negative, non-increasing Toeplitz coefficients, arXiv:2405.13763 Thm 2) is indeed violated at the default momentum once a schedule is attached, and _blt.py:185-192 evaluates it with skip_checks=True. BUT this is the same defect, same call site, and same fix as OPEN issue #595, whose acceptance criterion ('BLT does not evaluate minsep_sensitivity_squared on coefficients that fail its own non-negativity / non-increasing check') is configuration-agnostic and resolves this case too; #595 already reports a larger 2.03x under-report, so this is not a materially worse instance. I also refuted the reachability half of the headline: the trainer does inject lr_schedule for mf_blt (_dpftrl.py:87,113-118), but mf_blt's only allowed sampler is balls_in_bins (_ALLOWED_SAMPLERS), and BallsInBins uses min_sep=num_bins (_balls_in_bins.py:98) and for BltStrategy routes through toeplitz_gram_matrix/bnb_mc_pld without ever calling strategy.sensitivity(). b_min_sep only accepts BandMfStrategy and poisson rejects BLT outright, so the affected path is reachable only through a bare mf_gaussian(nm, blt_strategy(lr_schedule=...), n_steps=N, min_sep=1, max_participations>1) call in the functional API -- narrower than 'the trainer does this automatically'. Severity medium and duplicate of #595.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A functional-API user builds blt_strategy(max_buffers=10, momentum=1.0, lr_schedule=linear_schedule(...)) -- momentum=1.0 is the default -- and accounts it with dpftrl_acc.mf_gaussian(nm, strategy, n_steps=20, min_sep=1). The optimized Toeplitz coefficients go negative (min -0.1604 linear, -0.1832 cosine) and non-monotone, so minsep_sensitivity_squared, called with skip_checks=True at _blt.py:185-192, is evaluated outside the hypothesis of Theorem 2 of arXiv:2405.13763 and stops being an upper bound: reported S = 1.86202 vs exhaustively-verified true S = 2.69864 (1.449x; cosine 1.75101 vs 2.69688, 1.540x). Since MfGaussian.pld sets effective_nm = nm / S, epsilon is under-reported. The gap vanishes at min_sep >= 2 (1.0001 at 2, 1.0000 at 3), and the HF trainer path is not affected at all: mf_blt is pinned to balls_in_bins, which uses min_sep = num_bins and, for BLT, reaches the PLD through toeplitz_gram_matrix/bnb_mc_pld without calling strategy.sensitivity(). This is the same defect and same fix as open issue #595, at a lower ratio than the 2.03x already recorded there.

verdicts.title: dpsgd_acc.adaclip's num_groups parameter is documented nowhere, including in its published signature, while per-group adaptive clipping is documented
verdicts.reasoning: Verified every link. _adaclip.py:37 declares num_groups: int = 1 on AdaClip and :104-108 on the adaclip() factory; the docstring at :30-32 says it accounts for K independent quantile queries under per-group adaptive clipping; :100-102 multiplies the bit PLD by num_groups and effective_noise_multiplier passes num_groups into _native.adaclip_sensitivity. 'grep -rn num_groups docs/' returns exactly two hits, both docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/band-mf.md:191 and :212, an unrelated BandMF group count -- so the parameter appears nowhere in the DP-SGD docs, and the published signatures at docs/reference/accounting.md:310 and docs/user-guide/accounting.md:185 both omit it, as does the recipe at docs/user-guide/clipping.md:230-249. Meanwhile docs/user-guide/clipping.md:455-473 documents 'Adaptive per-group clipping' with per_group(...), and the runtime confirms one released statistic per group: _adaptive.py:498-510 loops over sorted group names, folds a per-group RNG key, and adds noise to each group's rate separately. The charge is therefore genuinely K-fold and the documented recipe charges 1. Reproduced the reporter's numbers exactly: (poisson(adaclip(gaussian(1.0), fraction_noise_std=0.05, expected_batch_size=256, num_groups=g), 0.01)*1000).epsilon_at(1e-5) = 1.83116 (g=1), 1.83408 (2), 1.83701 (3), 1.85168 (8); I extended it to 1.87531 (16), 1.92321 (32), 2.02156 (64). Direction is non-conservative. Magnitude is small at realistic group counts (0.3-1.1% for 2-8 groups) but grows to ~10% at 64 groups, which per-layer grouping reaches. Not marked as tracked: the nearest issue, #345 ('Bind AdaClip's released statistic to the parameters the accountant charges'), lists 'groups' in one acceptance bullet, but it is a code-side design change (pass one runtime state object into accounting), it is closed as not_planned on GitHub (the tsv snapshot predates that), and no one working from it would touch the two doc signatures; the remediation here is disjoint and cheap.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user follows docs/user-guide/clipping.md:455-473 to run adaptive per-group clipping over G groups, then accounts for it with the recipe the same page publishes at :230-249 (or docs/reference/accounting.md:310, or docs/user-guide/accounting.md:185), none of which mentions num_groups. The runtime releases one independently-noised clipping rate per group each step (_adaptive.py:498-510), but the accountant composes a single quantile query, so epsilon is systematically under-charged. Measured at nm=1.0, q=0.01, 1000 steps, delta=1e-5: 1.83116 charged vs 1.83701 true at 3 groups, 1.85168 at 8, 1.87531 at 16, 1.92321 at 32, 2.02156 at 64 (about 10% under-charge). The parameter exists and works correctly; it is simply absent from every published signature, so a user cannot discover it.

verdicts.title: training-arguments.md publishes a mf_blt default (max_buffers=16) that is both wrong and rejected by the code, plus a wrong noise_calibration_kwargs default
verdicts.reasoning: All three factual claims verified. docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:143 publishes '{"max_buffers": 16}' as the mf_blt default, while _training_arguments.py:205-211 sets 'mf_blt': {'max_buffers': 10} with an inline comment stating the BLT math rejects > 15 as ill-conditioned. Reproduced the hard rejection: blt_strategy(max_buffers=16) constructs, but .sensitivity(n_steps=64, min_sep=8, max_participations=8) raises ValueError('max_buffers > 15 will likely cause numerical issues.'), while max_buffers=10 returns 5.109544420457363 -- so the documented default is not merely wrong, it is unusable, and docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/blt.md:191 publishes a '1 - 20' range with the same defect for 16-20. Second, training-arguments.md:129 states the noise_calibration_kwargs defaults are {'min': 0.01, ...} while _training_arguments.py:894 injects ('min', 0.11); docs/reference/transformers.md:186 correctly says 0.11, so the two reference pages contradict each other. Third, blt.md:190 lists an 'error' parameter ('max' or 'mean') that does not exist: inspect.signature(blt_strategy) is (*, max_buffers: int = 10, momentum: float = 1.0, lr_schedule: Schedule | None = None). No epsilon impact -- the max_buffers path fails loudly and a wider calibration bracket floor does not change the calibrated target -- so affects_epsilon=false is correct. Medium is justified by breadth (four separate factual errors across three pages, one of them a published default a user would copy into a config generator), not by severity of consequence. #419 ('Align transformer reference tables and defaults with dataclass fields'), the closest tracked work, is closed, so this is residual drift.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user reads docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:143, believes max_buffers=16 is the shipped mf_blt default, and pins it explicitly (or generates configs from the table). Reproduced: blt_strategy(max_buffers=16).sensitivity(n_steps=64, min_sep=8, max_participations=8) raises ValueError('max_buffers > 15 will likely cause numerical issues.'); the real default, 10, returns 5.109544420457363. docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/blt.md:191 publishes the range as '1 - 20', which is unusable for 16-20, and blt.md:190 lists an 'error' parameter that blt_strategy(*, max_buffers, momentum, lr_schedule) does not accept. Separately, training-arguments.md:129 documents a calibration floor of min=0.01 while the code injects 0.11 (_training_arguments.py:894) and docs/reference/transformers.md:186 documents 0.11 -- the two reference pages contradict. Everything fails loudly or is inert; no privacy number is misstated.

verdicts.title: Two documented sampling_mode values (sequential, cyclic_poisson) are accepted by no mechanism, and the reference table's override list omits the modes that are accepted
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced both halves. _SAMPLING_MODES (_training_arguments.py:154-164) does contain 'cyclic_poisson' and 'sequential' -- which is exactly the set training-arguments.md:124 publishes -- but _ALLOWED_SAMPLERS (:185-193) never lists either for any mechanism, so the second validation branch at :1047-1053 always rejects them. Confirmed by construction (with privacy_noise_multiplier set so the earlier calibration guard does not mask it): every one of gaussian/mf_band/mf_blt/mf_identity x sequential/cyclic_poisson raises "sampling_mode='...' is not valid for privacy_noise_mechanism='...'; allowed: [...]". The complement error is also real: docs/reference/transformers.md:179 lists only 'b_min_sep' for mf_band and only 'balls_in_bins' for mf_blt/bisr/bsr/lambda_cgd, but TrainingArguments accepts mf_band + poisson and mf_identity + balls_in_bins (both constructed successfully), and training-arguments.md:142 documents the mf_band/poisson pair -- so the two reference pages disagree on a privacy-relevant allow-list. Severity lowered to low: the rejection is fail-closed and the error message enumerates the allowed set, and the reference-page omission is a missing option rather than a wrong one. affects_epsilon=false is correct.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user picks sampling_mode='sequential' or 'cyclic_poisson' from the set published at training-arguments.md:124 and TrainingArguments always raises, e.g. "sampling_mode='sequential' is not valid for privacy_noise_mechanism='mf_blt'; allowed: ['balls_in_bins']" -- verified for all four of gaussian, mf_band, mf_blt, mf_identity and both values, because _ALLOWED_SAMPLERS contains neither anywhere. Conversely a reader of docs/reference/transformers.md:179 concludes mf_band pins b_min_sep and mf_identity pins poisson, while the code accepts mf_band+poisson and mf_identity+balls_in_bins (both verified to construct), and training-arguments.md:142 documents the mf_band+poisson pair -- the two reference pages contradict each other on a privacy-relevant sampler allow-list. All failures are loud and the error names the valid options.
